Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Denominations and Characteristics of Coins
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 24th July 2009 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

Milled and bearing the words “MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE” and lion symbol.
The Singapore Arms in the centre with the yeardate “2009” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock of the coin.
The coin design draws inspiration from the 2009 National Day theme “Come Together — Reaching Out Reaching Up”, based on our pledge as the anchoring idea.
At the heart of the coin are a man and a woman taking the Pledge before the Singapore flag to symbolise the coming together as “one united people”; to support one another regardless of “race, language or religion”.

The Singapore Arms in the centre with the yeardate “2009” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin.
On the right, stylised human figures reaching up into the sky in different colours that match the five stars in the 2009 National Day Parade (NDP) logo reflect the second aspect of this year’s National Day theme, i.e., reaching up towards our hopes and aspirations.
The tag line in the 2009 NDP logo, i.e., “Reaching Out Reaching Up”, underpins a stylised version of the Marina Bay’s floating platform, the venue of this year’s NDP in celebration of our 44 years of independence.
The denomination is at the top of the coin.
